name: nats
title: Nats
description: Send and receive messages from NATS messaging system.
label: messaging

properties.name: topic
properties.description: The name of topic we want to use

properties.name: connectionTimeout
properties.label: common
properties.description: Timeout for connection attempts. (in milliseconds)

properties.name: flushConnection
properties.label: common
properties.description: Define if we want to flush connection when stopping or not

properties.name: flushTimeout
properties.label: common
properties.description: Set the flush timeout (in milliseconds)

properties.name: jetstreamEnabled
properties.label: common
properties.description: Sets whether to enable JetStream support for this endpoint.

properties.name: jetstreamName
properties.label: common
properties.description: Sets the name of the JetStream stream to use.

properties.name: maxPingsOut
properties.label: common
properties.description: maximum number of pings have not received a response allowed by the client

properties.name: maxReconnectAttempts
properties.description: Max reconnection attempts

properties.name: noEcho
properties.description: Turn off echo. If supported by the gnatsd version you are connecting to this flag will prevent the server from echoing messages back to the connection if it has subscriptions on the subject being published to.

properties.name: noRandomizeServers
properties.description: Whether or not randomizing the order of servers for the connection attempts

properties.name: pedantic
properties.label: common
properties.description: Whether or not running in pedantic mode (this affects performance)

properties.name: pingInterval
properties.description: Ping interval to be aware if connection is still alive (in milliseconds)

properties.name: reconnect
properties.label: common
properties.description: Whether or not using reconnection feature

properties.name: reconnectTimeWait
properties.label: common
properties.description: Waiting time before attempts reconnection (in milliseconds)

properties.name: requestCleanupInterval
properties.label: common
properties.description: Interval to clean up cancelled/timed out requests.

properties.name: servers
properties.label: common
properties.description: URLs to one or more NAT servers. Use comma to separate URLs when specifying multiple servers.

properties.name: verbose
properties.description: Whether or not running in verbose mode

properties.name: ackPolicy
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Acknowledgement mode. none = Messages are acknowledged as soon as the server sends them (danger: messages that Camel failed to process is also ack). Clients do not need to ack. all = All messages with a sequence number less than the message acked are also acknowledged. E.g. reading a batch of messages 1..100. Ack on message 100 will acknowledge 1..99 as well. explicit (default) = Each message is acknowledged individually by Camel after the message has been processed, this ensures the message is only ack if success and nack if processing failed due to an exception during routing. Message can be acked out of sequence and create gaps of unacknowledged messages in the consumer.

properties.name: ackWait
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: After a message is delivered to a consumer, the server waits 30 seconds (default) for an acknowledgement. If none arrives (timeout), the message becomes eligible for redelivery.

properties.name: durableName
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets the name to assign to the JetStream durable consumer. Setting this value makes the consumer durable. The value is used to set the durable() field in the underlying NATS ConsumerConfiguration.Builder.

properties.name: manualAck
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Whether to allow doing manual acknowledgment via NatsManualAck. If this option is enabled then an instance of NatsManualAck is stored on the org.apache.camel.Exchange message header, which allows end users to access this API and perform manual ack/nak/term operations via the JetStream consumer. When enabled, the automatic acknowledgment on exchange completion is disabled. If the user does not call any ack method, the message remains unacknowledged and NATS will redeliver it after the ackWait timeout expires. This option is only applicable when JetStream is enabled (jetstreamEnabled=true). It has no effect when ackPolicy=None since the server acknowledges messages automatically on delivery.

properties.name: maxDeliver
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Maximum number of attempts to deliver a message from Nats to a consumer. Once MaxDeliver is reached, the NATS server stops attempting to deliver that specific message. The message is not deleted, it remains in the stream but is simply skipped. It is recommended to set this option to a sensible value in case a message is poison and can not successfully be processed and would always keep failing.

properties.name: maxMessages
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Stop receiving messages from a topic we are subscribing to after maxMessages

properties.name: nackWait
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: For negative acknowledgements (NAK), redelivery is delayed by 5 seconds (default). Setting this to 0 or negative makes the redelivery immediately. Be careful as this can cause the consumer to keep re-processing the same message over and over again due to intermediate error that last a while.

properties.name: poolSize
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Consumer thread pool size (default is 10)

properties.name: pullBatchSize
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Maximum number of messages to fetch per pull request when using a JetStream Pull Subscription. Only used when {code pullSubscription=true}.

properties.name: pullFetchTimeout
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Maximum time (in milliseconds) to wait for a batch of messages to be available on the server during a single fetch when using a JetStream Pull Subscription. Only used when {code pullSubscription=true}.

properties.name: pullSubscription
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets the consumer subscription type for JetStream. Set to true to use a Pull Subscription (consumer explicitly requests messages). Set to false to use a Push Subscription (messages are automatically delivered).

properties.name: queueName
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The Queue name if we are using nats for a queue configuration

properties.name: replyToDisabled
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Can be used to turn off sending back reply message in the consumer.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: consumerConfiguration
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets a custom ConsumerConfiguration object for the JetStream consumer. This is an advanced option typically used when you need to configure properties not exposed as simple Camel URI parameters. When set, this object will be used to build the final consumer subscription options.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: replySubject
properties.label: producer
properties.description: the subject to which subscribers should send response

properties.name: requestTimeout
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Request timeout in milliseconds

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: connection
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Reference an already instantiated connection to Nats server

properties.name: headerFilterStrategy
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use a custom header filter strategy.

properties.name: jetstreamAsync
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Sets whether to operate JetStream requests asynchronously.

properties.name: traceConnection
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Whether or not connection trace messages should be printed to standard out for fine grained debugging of connection issues.

properties.name: credentialsFilePath
properties.label: security
properties.description: If we use useCredentialsFile to true we'll need to set the credentialsFilePath option. It can be loaded by default from classpath, but you can prefix with classpath:, file:, or http: to load the resource from different systems.

properties.name: secure
properties.label: security
properties.description: Set secure option indicating TLS is required

properties.name: sslContextParameters
properties.label: security
properties.description: To configure security using SSLContextParameters
